# Evidence synthesis: termenv-preserve-ansi-resets

## Coverage and interpretation

This audit covers all **five supplied source files** in group `termenv-preserve-ansi-resets`, batch 1 of 1: two student trajectories and three teacher trajectories, represented by six audit chunks. The reports describe complete model-reviewed chunks; this synthesis uses their cited observations and supplied inventories, not a fresh inspection of raw files. File counts include copies and must not be treated as independent trials. In particular, the two similarly structured guidance traces do not establish two independent student outcomes.

The original task prompt is not visible in these reports. The coding goal—ANSI-aware truncation and preservation of enclosing styles across embedded resets—is inferred from the trajectories. Formal scores not supplied are **unknown**. Blank CLI usage fields mean unavailable or unlinked, not zero; historical model cost cannot be recovered from their absence.

## Evidence matrix

Event references are to `main_agent` in the original source identified in each row; inventory results are explicitly identified as such.

| Source and original path | Observed work and validation | Outcome and limits |
|---|---|---|
| **H0006**, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-baseline-run/runs/baseline_ds1017_termenv_a1_vm8_20261120_r1/infer_logs/termenv-preserve-ansi-resets/turn_1/trajs.json` | Created and revised ANSI utilities and integrations; intermediate invariant and regression tests exposed problems (events 51–57, 107–113, 153–166). Commit recorded at event 231. | Nonempty patch; inventory reports **solved**, 35/35 fail-to-pass and 87/87 pass-to-pass. Evaluation contents were not shown. Teacher receipt is unknown. |
| **H0031**, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_integration_01/codex_integration_01_shared/hint_gen/termenv-preserve-ansi-resets/trajs.json` | Teacher inspected a reference diff and repository, then wrote a guide (events 1–18); returned it at event 19. | Guidance completed; no implementation, tests, student receipt or adoption observed. Coding outcome unknown. |
| **H0032**, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_integration_02/codex_integration_02_H/reviews/termenv-preserve-ansi-resets/round_1/teacher/trajs.json` | Reviewer inspected selected repository facts and wrote a review (events 1–4). Event 5 reports student work and labels the trajectory “USED.” | Those student operations and original hint delivery are not independently visible here. Review completion is not coding success; adoption and formal outcome are unknown. |
| **H0033**, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_integration_02/codex_integration_02_H_r1/infer_logs/termenv-preserve-ansi-resets/turn_1/trajs.json` | After a recovered branch error, implemented and tested ANSI and integration changes; committed at event 24 (events 1–24). | Nonempty patch; inventory reports **solved**, 35/35 fail-to-pass and 87/87 pass-to-pass. Hint paths were available, but receipt and adoption are unknown. |
| **H0036**, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_integration_02/codex_integration_02_shared/hint_gen/termenv-preserve-ansi-resets/trajs.json` | Teacher inspected a reference and existing APIs, diagnosed possible risks, and wrote and returned guidance (events 2–19). | Guidance session completed; no implementation, testing, student continuation or receipt observed. Coding outcome unknown. |

## Attempts, stops and observed behavior

Both visible student attempts produced substantial patches and have reported formal success. H0006’s inventory lists a 19,675-byte patch; its recorded amended commit changed seven files (event 231). Build, vet and existing tests ran, and build and tests ran again after a comment-only amendment (events 210–211, 230–231). Temporary tests had been removed, leaving no test files in the new `ansi` package at the final run. The inventory scores support the reported evaluation result, but the underlying evaluation file and all edge cases are not independently visible.

H0006 also demonstrates why an intermediate failure is not the same as a failed final attempt. A strict width invariant failed when a one-cell tail was used at width zero; the student relaxed the invariant rather than changing that behavior (events 107–113). A later change incorrectly truncated a fitting string with a tail; a test caught it and a guard was added (events 153–166). Thus the eventual passing checks establish what their final assertions tested, not that the original strict width property holds. Whether an oversized tail or replay of deduplicated raw style sequences is correct under the unseen contract remains unresolved.

H0033’s initial branch creation from `main` failed because the reference was absent; the student successfully branched from `master` instead (events 1–10). A before/after reproduction changed from an embedded reset without restored bold and an incorrect visible width of 5, to restored bold and width 2. Build, existing tests and a temporary script also passed (events 17–18, 21–24). The temporary script was removed, and the new package had no committed test files. The visible ASCII truncation implementation discarded the requested tail, and its check expected that output (events 15, 23); whether this matches the original specification is unknown, not an established defect.

Operational restrictions are distinct from algorithmic results. In H0006, upstream-reference and module-version lookups were denied (events 17–18, 27–28), but work continued to normal completion. H0033’s missing-branch error was similarly recovered. Its inventory records a parent status of `stopped` alongside student terminal reason `end_turn`; the visible student trace does not establish that the student attempt was technically interrupted. No separate terminal CLI stop or failed final implementation is established in these five files.

Nor is an empty implementation patch established. H0031’s confirmed guide-file creation had an empty `structuredPatch`, but that was not an attempted task-code patch (events 17–18). H0031 and H0036 are guidance-only traces; H0032 is a review-only trace. Their lack of a visible code patch or formal score cannot be converted into a failed, partial, interrupted, or successful coding attempt.

## Teacher roles, adoption and transferable constraints

H0031 and H0036 inspected reference diffs without applying them. Both produced advice about control-sequence handling, reset restoration, propagation and tests; their concerns about reference-parser and ASCII behavior were diagnoses or hypotheses, not executed fixes or validated failures (H0031 events 1–2, 17–19; H0036 events 2, 17–19). Their successful session statuses indicate completion of guidance, not acceptance or independent quality of an implementation.

H0033’s inventory lists available hint and teacher-state paths, while H0006 links a system-prompt archive. The reports do not show captured prompt text or delivered teacher events establishing receipt in either student trace. H0032’s after-round review was not input to that round: its “USED” label and reported student alignment are second-hand observations, and the reviewer acknowledged that alignment does not prove causal reasoning (event 5). Consequently, neither advice adoption nor its absence is established for the student attempts. The two reported student successes do not support a causal superiority claim about guidance.

The transferable constraint is evidentiary: distinguish a proposal from an executed update, a local check from formal evaluation, and an available artifact from received advice. The traces also show that explicit invariants and before/after reproductions can expose behavior, but H0006’s relaxed invariant and H0033’s contract-dependent ASCII expectation are counterexamples to treating passing checks as exhaustive proof. ANSI reset state, hyperlink closure, grapheme widths and ASCII handling are task-specific; their remaining edge cases are hypotheses, not established failures.

No Scene task appears in this batch. Advice receipt, diagnosis, execution, acceptance and independently observed quality for Scene are therefore **not applicable**, rather than silently assumed. This is an audit-only historical synthesis, not a source of new solutions, skills or test feedback.
